mcp-tools-renderer.ts: exports renderMcpToolsTable(tools: McpToolEntry[]): string — typed port filtering note_only: true entries. Output is structurally identical to the JS original.

role-validator.ts: exports validateRole(role, manifestRoles): ValidationResult[] and validateNoteOnlyGuard(output, mcpTools): ValidationResult[] — both with full TypeScript types. validateRole warns when a persona role is absent from the workflow manifest; validateNoteOnlyGuard errors when a note_only tool leaks into rendered output.

comments.note: CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS is defined as a module-private const in frontmatter-templates.ts and inlined into FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC via template literal. AC-3 (role-validator.ts): validateRole and validateNoteOnlyGuard both exported with full TypeScript types. validateRole accepts ReadonlyArray<string> | ReadonlySet<string> and returns correct ValidationResult[] in all tested cases. validateNoteOnlyGuard uses escapeRegExp for safe regex construction and correctly detects leakage of note_only tools into rendered output. comments.note: AC-3 signature deviation: The WP spec describes validateNoteOnlyGuard(output) as a single-parameter function, but the implementation is validateNoteOnlyGuard(output, mcpTools). This deviation is architecturally sound — the function cannot detect note_only leakage without the tools list. The Developer documented this clearly in both implementation comments and handoff notes. The WP-002 factory will call it correctly via the onValidate hook. This is a low-risk WP spec imprecision, not a functional defect.

escapeRegExp in role-validator.ts correctly escapes all standard regex special characters. Verified: tool names containing dots (e.g. tool.with.dots) are escaped to tool\.with\.dots preventing false positive matches on similarly-structured names.

No code smells, anti-patterns, or type-safety issues detected. All four files are pure functions with no side effects, no file-system I/O, and no global state. Consistent with the design intent documented in the module JSDoc headers.

summary: Reviewed all four source files in src/plugins/ledger/ of ai-persona-builder-STABLE: roster-renderer.ts, mcp-tools-renderer.ts, role-validator.ts, frontmatter-templates.ts.
Architecture: All four files are pure functions with no side effects, no file-system I/O, no global mutable state. Design is correct and consistent with the module isolation intent.
roster-renderer.ts: Logic is byte-identical to persona-helpers.js renderRoster(). RosterEntry interface is well-typed. JSDoc is exemplary, including a worked @example. No issues.
mcp-tools-renderer.ts: Logic is byte-identical to persona-helpers.js renderMcpToolsTable(). McpToolEntry interface accurately models the YAML source with correct optional flag. No issues.

role-validator.ts: validateRole correctly normalises ReadonlyArray/ReadonlySet to a Set before the has() lookup — no O(n) linear scans. validateNoteOnlyGuard uses escapeRegExp (covers all standard regex special characters: .*+?^${}()|[]\) before constructing the RegExp, matching the detection pattern from build-personas.js. Import of ValidationResult from '../types.js' resolves correctly via ESM .js extension convention.

Signature deviation (validateNoteOnlyGuard): WP spec lists a one-parameter signature; implementation takes (output, mcpTools). This deviation is architecturally necessary — the function cannot enumerate note_only tool names without the tools array. The WP-002 factory is the caller and will supply both arguments via its onValidate closure. Reviewer confirms this is acceptable; the WP spec was imprecise, not the implementation.

frontmatter-templates.ts: FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE and FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC are structurally identical to their counterparts in build-personas.js. CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS inlining produces a byte-identical expansion to the runtime return of ccFrontmatterFields(). Template variables and conditionals are preserved exactly. Both exports are typed as string constants.
Type safety: All public exports carry explicit TypeScript types. No use of 'any'. Imports use 'import type' where appropriate (ValidationResult, McpToolEntry cross-module import).

Plugin interface compatibility: The onValidate hook signature in runner.ts is (persona, suite) → ValidationResult[]. The validators in role-validator.ts are pure helpers called by the WP-002 factory — they are not directly exposed as hook implementations. This is the correct layering pattern.
Build verification confirmed by QA (tsc --noEmit exit 0, 227 regression tests pass). Node.js not available in review sandbox — no re-run attempted; QA results accepted as authoritative.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met. Code quality is high. PASS.

comments.note: role-validator.ts: The Set normalisation (Array→Set) happens on every call to validateRole. For the typical use case (one call per persona per build run) this is negligible. If the factory were to call validateRole in a tight loop it would be worth hoisting the Set construction to the factory's onSuiteInit phase. This is not a current concern — just a note for WP-002 factory design.

frontmatter-templates.ts: CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS is declared with a leading backtick template but contains no interpolation — a plain string literal would be equivalent. The template literal is not incorrect; it keeps the indentation visually consistent with the surrounding templates. No change required.

No cross-module re-export yet (no ledger/index.ts) — intentional per WP-002 scope boundary. Downstream consumers cannot import from '@mistralys/persona-builder/plugins/ledger' until WP-002 delivers the barrel. This is by design.
